summary: Lothar Ledderose worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. He served as professor at Heidelberg (~1976–2010) and president of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

Lothar von Falkenhausen specializes in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn, Peking University, and Harvard University. In 1993, he became a full professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, later serving as associate director (2004–2011).

Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at several French institutions under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Alain Froment. He taught at Oxford (1951–1955) and became Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études/EHESS in 1955.

Louis Finot worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes and under Sylvain Lévi. His key appointments included director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1898) and professor at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Around 1980, he held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient.

Louis H. Gray worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (1921).

Louis Havet was a linguistics scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and chairman of Latin philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and other Paris institutions. He held posts at the EPHE (~1928–1954) and as professor at the University of Paris (~1937–1966).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Liège, Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden under mentors including Sylvain Lévi and Hendrik Kern. He was a professor at Ghent (1893–1929) and Brussels (~1921–1935).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as administrator at INALCO (~1795–1824) and chief keeper of manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1795–1824).

Louise Allison Cort is a scholar in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College. She served as a ceramics curator at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from circa 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under Sibnath Sarma, also studying under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University, completing his PhD under Jan Gonda. He served as an assistant at the University of Groningen (1968–1971).
Lozang Samten studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University (~1978–1983) and later held a post there around 1990.

Luca Maria Olivieri is an archaeology and Indology scholar who earned his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin. He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~2011) and was associate professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2020–2021).

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held posts as a lecturer in Japanese religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015) at SOAS University of London.
Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford, where she also held an academic post.
